science.title: Edge-attentive graph residual learning for aircraft surface-field prediction under rudder deflection
science.description: Rudder deflection complicates aerodynamic surrogate modeling by altering both surface geometry and the flow response. This study proposes an edge-attentive graph residual framework for predicting the pressure coefficient and wall vorticity magnitude over a simplified full-size external aircraft configuration based on the general aerodynamic layout of the F-22 under varying flight conditions and rudder deflections. Rudder surfaces are aligned with a reference configuration, and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) surface fields are resampled onto a common template mesh to establish consistent node ordering and connectivity. A multilayer perceptron (MLP) provides an initial point-wise prediction from operating parameters and nodal geometric features. A graph residual branch refines this prediction using mesh connectivity and geometric edge features, with attention weights determined by nodal and edge states. Five models are compared using steady compressible RANS CFD data: MLP, GNS, MLP-GNS, MLP-GNS-Equal with equal normalized neighbor weights, and Hybrid with learned edge attention. On the test set, Hybrid reduces the mean absolute error by 60.4% for pressure coefficient prediction and 46.0% for wall vorticity magnitude prediction relative to MLP. It also gives the lowest 95th and 99th percentiles of absolute error. Surface-field comparisons show that Hybrid more closely agrees with the RANS CFD reference in localized pressure transitions and high-vorticity regions under the tested configuration and operating conditions.

science.title: Characterization of fungal communities and postharvest aroma alterations induced by Botrytis cinerea in Taif rose (Rosa damascena) petals
science.description: This study investigated the culturable fungal community associated with Rosa damascena petals collected from commercial rose farms in the Taif region, Saudi Arabia, and evaluated the effects of Botrytis cinerea infection on fungal community composition, floral aroma, and volatile organic compound (VOC) profiles. Fungi were isolated using culture-dependent methods, identified by ITS-rDNA sequencing and phylogenetic analysis, while fungal community diversity, correlations between fungal abundance and distribution, and infection-induced community shifts were evaluated using ecological indices, Pearson and Spearman correlation analyses, linear regression, and non-metric multidimensional scaling (NMDS). Sensory evaluation, gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC–MS), and metal oxide semiconductor (MOS) electronic nose analyses were used to assess aroma deterioration and VOC changes. A total of 18 fungal taxa representing nine genera were identified, with Cladosporium cladosporioides (90% isolation frequency) and Alternaria alternata (80%) dominating the petal mycobiota, whereas B. cinerea (15%) and Penicillium expansum (35%) were consistently recovered from symptomatic petals. Mean colony recovery was strongly correlated with isolation frequency (Pearson’s r = 0.90; Spearman’s ρ = 0.88; p < 0.001), and NMDS analysis (stress = 0.14) demonstrated significant shifts in fungal community structure following B. cinerea infection. Infected petals exhibited marked deterioration in aroma quality, including approximately 57–69% reductions in floral intensity and freshness, a significant increase in musty off-odour (F = 32.1, p < 0.001), decreased concentrations of the major floral monoterpenes geraniol (− 62%) and citronellol (− 71%), and a 15-fold increase in the fungal-associated volatile 1-octen-3-ol. Linear regression demonstrated strong relationships between VOC composition and sensory quality, while the MOS electronic nose classified healthy and infected petals with 95.2% accuracy. These findings demonstrate that B. cinerea infection substantially alters the petal mycobiota, VOC composition, and sensory quality, highlighting the potential of VOC-based approaches as complementary, rapid, and non-destructive tools for monitoring gray mold development and supporting postharvest quality management of Taif rose.

science.title: The selective impact of tobacco genotypes on the microbial diversity and structure in the rhizosphere during the floating seedling cultivation
science.description: Rhizosphere microorganisms are crucial for plant growth, development, and stress adaptation, and plant genotype can shape rhizosphere microbial communities through genotype-dependent differences in root traits and rhizodeposition. In this study, three cultivated tobacco varieties, Yunyan 87 (YY87), K326, and Honghuadajinyuan (HD), one local variety, Chuanpihongda (CP), and one wild species, Nicotiana repanda (YS), were selected to investigate temporal changes in rhizosphere bacterial and fungal communities under a floating seedling system. The results showed significant differences in bacterial and fungal alpha diversity between tobacco genotypes and the unseeded control. Specifically, bacterial diversity in all tobacco varieties exceeded that of the unseeded control only in the later stages of cultivation, whereas fungal diversity in these varieties consistently remained higher than that of the control throughout the entire period. PCoA and PERMANOVA indicated that both genotype and sampling time significantly affected bacterial and fungal community composition, with sampling time explaining a larger proportion of variation. At the phylum level, bacterial communities were mainly dominated by Pseudomonadota, Bacillota, Actinomycetota, Chloroflexota, and Acidobacteriota, whereas fungal communities were mainly represented by Ascomycota, Basidiomycota, Chytridiomycota, and Mucoromycota. Genotype-associated differences were also observed at the genus level and in co-occurrence network patterns. Functional prediction suggested that metabolism-related categories were dominant across samples, and CP showed relatively higher predicted abundances of several metabolic pathways, including terpenoid and polyketide metabolism. These findings provide a reference for understanding genotype-associated rhizosphere microbial variation in tobacco floating seedling systems and for future studies on microbial regulation during seedling production.
